userStory: As a person working across SkooleeAI modules, I want consistent navigation and task patterns so that I can complete school work without relearning controls or searching through irrelevant modules.
problem: The current app supplies violet branding, role shells and reusable components, but repeated local patterns and historical accessibility findings show drift. Retain recognizable branding while improving task hierarchy, contrast and predictability. A large global catalogue must not create an equally large navigation burden: teachers, families, support staff and institutional leaders need different default workspaces with shared interaction rules underneath.
scope: Define design tokens for neutral surfaces, solid readable text, restrained violet actions, spacing, typography, focus and status colors.
Specify role-based information architecture with stable primary navigation, local module navigation and enabled-module filtering.
Standardize forms, data tables, task queues, dialogs, confirmation, skeletons, feedback and responsive page headers.
Build documented reference compositions for staff productivity and family/student mobile tasks using synthetic data.
Migrate priority workflows through component-level accessibility and visual regression checks rather than isolated cosmetic overrides.
Publish ownership and contribution rules so new features reuse the system and document justified exceptions.
outOfScope: A brand replacement or a decorative dashboard redesign disconnected from task completion.
Displaying all global capabilities to every role or forcing mobile tables into unreadable miniature layouts.
acceptance: Each supported role has a documented primary navigation with visible active state and no links to unavailable modules.
Reference pages use shared tokens and components for headings, actions, validation, dialogs and empty states.
Text contrast and focus visibility pass the agreed accessibility checks across default, disabled and error states.
Forms preserve labels, help and errors consistently, and tables offer keyboard-operable selection and actions.
Family/student pages remain usable at narrow phone width without horizontal page scrolling.
New feature reviews identify reused components and any approved exceptions before implementation.
qa: Complete equivalent create/edit/review actions in admissions, reports and fees and compare interaction consistency.
Navigate a family account with only two enabled modules at phone width and increased text size.
Switch an Arabic role shell between task list, form and dialog using keyboard only.
successMetric: Measure task completion and navigation errors on representative role journeys; track shared-component adoption and accessibility regressions.

principles: Use violet for primary action and selected context, with calm neutral work surfaces.
One clear primary action per task surface; secondary actions remain discoverable but quieter.
Let roles determine navigation and density while preserving familiar control behavior.

screens.name: Staff workspace reference
screens.purpose: A reusable staff composition presents the current scope, the next useful work and contextual navigation. This is a design reference for implementation, not a claim that synthetic activity reflects a real school.

screens.name: Form pattern reference
screens.purpose: The reference form demonstrates durable labels, section hierarchy, contextual help, a concise review summary and validation. The designer must show exactly how keyboard focus and recovery work rather than only a pristine empty form.

states.empty: Every module explains the absence of records and offers only an authorized useful next action.
states.loading: Use layout-matched panel skeletons while retaining navigation and already loaded context.
states.error: Errors explain the failed task, preserve input and offer a bounded recovery action.
states.permission: Hide unavailable navigation but explain direct-link denials without confidential details.
states.success: Confirm the real completed action with a source link; avoid generic celebration blocking the next task.

ux.mobile: Define family/student layouts from phone tasks first; staff tables use responsive priority columns or cards while retaining efficient desktop density.
ux.rtl: Use logical CSS properties, mirrored directional icons and explicit bidirectional isolation for identifiers, emails, equations and numeric values.
ux.accessibility: Require semantic controls, visible focus, keyboard parity, accessible names, adequate targets, readable contrast and reduced-motion support on reference flows.
copy: Changes saved. Review the updated record.
Choose a campus to continue.

userStory: As a school administrator, I want every school, campus and child relationship checked consistently so that staff and families receive exactly the records their current responsibilities permit.
problem: The main dashboard uses explicit pupil links, while the AI context still includes full-name matching and broader result reads. These are source concerns requiring verification, not demonstrated production exploits. Independently implemented guards also make future modules difficult to review. Central policy must express institutional scope, active membership, action and record relationship, while keeping forbidden identities out of error messages. The two operational screens are optional runbook or review-tool visualizations; delivery may use existing dashboards, CI reports or documented procedures rather than building new application panels.
scope: Define role/action/resource policies with explicit school and campus membership, guardianship and pupil-account relationships.
Build shared resolvers for APIs, server actions, AI context, exports and notifications; remove name-based ownership fallbacks.
Require current authorization at read and mutation time, including staff reassignment and multi-campus membership changes.
Add denied-access audit metadata without logging confidential record contents or revealing another family in the response.
Maintain a synthetic adversarial matrix covering different schools, campuses, classes, guardians and published versus draft results.
outOfScope: Changes to the commercial role names or manifest dependencies.
Giving school users a new security debugging console.
acceptance: Two pupils sharing a full name never become interchangeable in dashboard, AI, report, fee or export requests.
A parent requesting an unrelated child receives a consistent denial without that child’s name or existence details.
Campus-limited staff cannot expand scope through query parameters, nested writes, search, attachments or background job identifiers.
Published-result rules apply to family-facing AI context as well as ordinary result endpoints.
All tested public entry points use the shared policy or an explicitly documented service identity with equivalent restrictions.
An authorized administrator can inspect a permission decision using synthetic fixtures without accessing another tenant’s real records.
qa: Try the same namesake pupil fixture through portal, AI context and report download.
Reassign a teacher while their tab is open and repeat old-campus requests.
Submit a bulk request containing one valid record and one cross-school identifier.
successMetric: Zero unauthorized disclosures or mutations in the versioned adversarial matrix; track policy coverage for every newly added entry point.

principles: Operational screens belong to authorized internal reviewers, never pupil navigation.
Explain permissions in school language while showing technical decision detail only in the operator drill-down.
Keep the school and campus under test visible throughout a review.

screens.name: Access review
screens.purpose: Internal release workspace comparing expected and actual decisions for a selected synthetic persona. It should reveal policy inconsistency without turning protected school records into support browsing material.
notes: Decision details open beside the matrix

screens.name: Decision detail
screens.purpose: Show which relationship and publication rules produced a decision, the policy version and affected entry points. A failed check links to implementation evidence rather than offering an override.

states.empty: No policy runs yet; offer the seeded matrix and explain its synthetic scope.
states.loading: Keep the persona and previous run visible while individual checks complete.
states.error: Preserve completed checks and give a redacted run reference with retry for failed infrastructure.
states.permission: Hide the tool from school roles; reject direct access and avoid exposing fixture identities outside authorized review.
states.success: Show coverage, failures and evidence timestamp; completion never implies certification.

ux.mobile: On narrow operator screens show one case per card, with expected and actual decisions adjacent and details in a full-screen sheet.
ux.rtl: Mirror reading order; isolate policy IDs and paths as LTR so operators can copy exact identifiers.
ux.accessibility: All checks have text outcomes, table headers and keyboard access; focus returns to the inspected case after closing details.
copy: This account cannot access that record.
All 24 synthetic access checks passed.

userStory: As a school owner or invited staff member, I want sign-in, invitation, recovery and account removal to behave predictably so that legitimate access is easy and lost privileges stop immediately.
problem: Current helpers differ in whether they check active account and current role, while staff removal updates an activity flag. Historical logout tests do not establish every lifecycle path. Add consistent session invalidation and administrator MFA without stranding schools when an authenticator or recovery email is unavailable. Recovery must prove control without revealing whether an arbitrary email belongs to a pupil.
scope: Unify invitation states, expiry, resend and acceptance with role/campus details visible before account activation.
Invalidate relevant sessions after deactivation, role/campus change and sensitive recovery; check current membership server-side.
Add administrator MFA enrollment, verification, recovery codes and clearly audited recovery handling.
Show users their active sessions with device/time information and a revoke action, using cautious location claims.
Define email delivery failure and expired-link recovery paths with rate limits and generic unauthenticated responses.
outOfScope: Enterprise SSO protocol implementation, owned by the identity integration feature.
SMS as a mandatory second factor or automatic account recovery through support impersonation.
acceptance: An invitation can be accepted once within its validity period and cannot silently assign a different school or role.
Existing sessions lose revoked privileges on the next protected request, including server actions and AI routes.
Administrators finish MFA setup only after a successful challenge and acknowledgement of recovery instructions.
Recovery codes are single-use and never retrievable as plaintext after the initial protected presentation.
Expired invites preserve a clear route to request a new link without creating duplicate users.
Failed MFA or delivery attempts expose useful recovery actions without leaking account existence.
qa: Deactivate a signed-in teacher and attempt marks entry, messaging and report export.
Use one recovery code twice from separate browser sessions.
Accept an expired invitation after the administrator changes the intended campus.
successMetric: Measure invitation completion and recovery success; require all session-revocation paths to pass before enabling real school accounts.

principles: Show institution and role before asking a person to accept access.
Avoid security jargon and retain progress when verification fails.
Separate a reversible resend from a consequential revoke action.

screens.name: Account access
screens.purpose: School administrators manage invitations and active access without confusing staff employment records with login privileges. Each row exposes its actual state, intended campus and next permissible action.

screens.name: Protect your account
screens.purpose: An administrator verifies an authenticator and stores a recovery method before privileged access is enabled. The page explains what happens if the device is lost, with no forced abandonment of setup.

states.empty: No invited people; explain who can be invited and make role/campus required.
states.loading: Keep entered email and selected role while the invitation request completes.
states.error: Show a resend or verification retry with preserved input; never mark an undelivered invite accepted.
states.permission: Explain when only an institutional administrator can change access and provide a safe contact path.
states.success: Confirm which sessions ended or invitation was sent, with timestamp and next step.

ux.mobile: MFA and invitation acceptance are single-column mobile flows with large code inputs; account tables become concise person cards.
ux.rtl: Arabic guidance mirrors normally; email addresses, one-time codes and recovery codes remain isolated LTR.
ux.accessibility: Codes support paste, accessible labels and announced validation; do not force separate character boxes or rely on timed animations.
copy: Your invitation has expired. Request a new link.
Access removed. Existing sessions will need to sign in again.

userStory: As a principal, I want to approve an exact report version before families can see or receive it so that a later edit cannot silently change an already approved result.
problem: The bulk report path checks individual remarks, but a single-send path overrides approval after checking exam publication. Exam-state transitions do not prove every remark was approved. These source inconsistencies require a shared invariant, versioned content and fresh tests. Reviewers need to understand the changes they approve, while families need one clearly current published report and an understandable correction notice.
scope: Create report versions capturing marks, grading rules, remarks, language and generated document identity at approval time.
Centralize review, publication, PDF/export and delivery eligibility; remove caller-supplied approval overrides.
Invalidate approval after any material content change and retain prior published versions in restricted history.
Provide a class review queue with blockers, changed sections and batch approval only for individually eligible versions.
Make delivery reference the exact published version and give families a clear superseded/corrected status.
outOfScope: Changing the school’s grading policy or permitting AI to approve final results.
Replacing the existing examination lifecycle with a separate publication system.
acceptance: A report lacking approved remarks cannot be published or sent through bulk, individual, API or background paths.
Editing approved marks or remarks creates a new reviewable version and does not mutate the old published artifact.
An approval records reviewer, time and content version, and is rejected if the version changes during review.
Families and AI explanations receive only an authorized published version, including through old links.
Repeated send requests for the same version do not produce duplicate logical deliveries.
A corrected release identifies its predecessor and reason without exposing internal review notes to families.
qa: Approve version two while another staff member edits a remark in parallel.
Attempt the current single-send override path against an unapproved report.
Open an old family PDF link after a corrected report is published.
successMetric: Zero deliveries of unapproved or mismatched versions; measure reviewer minutes per class and percentage blocked for meaningful corrections.

principles: Put approval blockers and changed content before decorative performance summaries.
Use explicit version labels and separate Approve from Publish.
Keep family-facing correction language factual and free of staff blame.

screens.name: Report review
screens.purpose: A principal sees the class release readiness and can inspect reports that need attention. Counts distinguish missing marks, unreviewed remarks and eligible versions so batch actions never conceal unfinished work.
notes: Show last reviewer beside each item

screens.name: Approve this version
screens.purpose: Compare the pending report with its last approved version and preview exactly what the family receives. The reviewer can return a specific section for correction without publishing partial changes.

states.empty: No reports generated; link to the eligible locked exam and state what must be completed first.
states.loading: Load report sections within the stable review layout; never show old values as the pending version.
states.error: If another edit arrives, stop approval and show the new changes with a fresh review action.
states.permission: Teachers can correct assigned drafts; only authorized reviewers see approval and publication controls.
states.success: Confirm the approved version and remaining class blockers, then offer release preview.

ux.mobile: Stack report comparison sections vertically with clearly labeled prior and pending values; keep approval summary reachable without side-by-side scrolling.
ux.rtl: Render each language version in its native direction while keeping marks, version identifiers and comparison arrows unambiguous.
ux.accessibility: Changes include text labels and not color alone; preview text is selectable, keyboard navigable and available outside the PDF.
copy: This report changed after approval. Review version 3.
Published version 3. Families will receive this version.

userStory: As a school buyer, I want product claims, plan limits and billing behavior to agree so that I can evaluate SkooleeAI and purchase without discovering a different promise inside the application.
problem: The reviewed marketing site and local plan configuration disagree on enrollment and AI-credit limits. The site described credit rollover while the reset path only clears usage. The founder reported no school customers at review time, so testimonials and measured savings require evidence before publication. This feature makes commercial truth a versioned product contract, not merely a copywriting cleanup, and preserves existing customer commitments when plans change. The two operational screens are optional runbook or review-tool visualizations; delivery may use existing dashboards, CI reports or documented procedures rather than building new application panels.
currentEvidence: Live website observations recorded in the review, not a current re-audit
scope: Create a versioned commercial catalogue for plan names, limits, allowances, renewal/rollover rules and regional presentation.
Drive marketing comparison, app billing, checkout and server entitlements from the same approved contract or generated artifact.
Audit testimonials, metrics, competitor statements and platform availability against permissioned supporting evidence.
Add clearly labeled shipped, pilot and planned capability states and avoid presenting assumptions as measured results.
Define plan-change and grandfathering behavior with migration previews, effective dates and understandable customer communication.
Add release checks comparing displayed plan data with enforced limits and credit-reset behavior.
outOfScope: Inventing customer evidence, legal guarantees or a universal global price without market validation.
Automatically changing existing subscriptions merely to match newly written marketing copy.
acceptance: A selected plan has identical relevant limits in marketing, signup, billing, checkout and server enforcement.
Credit allowance and rollover wording matches tested renewal behavior, including any explicit expiry rules.
Every customer quotation or measured outcome has a traceable source and publication permission, otherwise it is removed or labeled appropriately.
Planned capabilities are never represented as generally available in pricing or sales material.
Existing customer contracts retain their approved terms or receive an explicitly authorized change process.
A release check detects entitlement drift and blocks publication of mismatched commercial data.
qa: Compare free, paid and custom plans across signup, upgrade and quota-exceeded flows.
Run a monthly credit reset with unused allowance and compare the resulting balance to displayed policy.
Update plan limits while an existing school has grandfathered terms and an open checkout.
successMetric: Zero plan-contract discrepancies in release checks; track billing expectation complaints and claims with verified evidence.

principles: Explain limits in school terms and put variable-cost allowances next to their practical effect.
Distinguish measured evidence from calculators, examples and future intentions.
Make plan changes understandable without exposing internal tier identifiers.

screens.name: Plan contract review
screens.purpose: An internal commercial review compares one plan version across public and authenticated surfaces. It exposes mismatches before release and records who approved the wording and enforcement contract.

screens.name: Claims evidence
screens.purpose: Content owners review statements against their evidence and permitted presentation. Demonstration personas, assumed savings and future platform capabilities remain explicitly labeled instead of borrowing the appearance of customer proof.

states.empty: No approved contract; show current discrepancies and prevent new unreviewed commercial publication.
states.loading: Keep the selected version and last validation result visible during checks.
states.error: Identify the differing field and affected surfaces; preserve drafted wording for correction.
states.permission: Only designated commercial owners publish; engineering reviewers can validate without changing prices.
states.success: Record the approved contract version, effective date and verified publication surfaces.

ux.mobile: Buyer pricing is easy to compare on mobile with concise limits and expandable detail; internal validation tables become field comparison cards.
ux.rtl: Localize plan names and commercial explanations while isolating numeric allowances and currencies; avoid ambiguous translated rollover wording.
ux.accessibility: Pricing comparisons expose semantic headers and feature text; tooltips supplement rather than hide essential purchase conditions.
copy: Unused monthly allowance expires at renewal, as described in this plan.
This time-saving example is illustrative, not a measured customer result.

userStory: As a platform operator, I want reproducible upgrades and rehearsed restoration so that schools can recover after a deployment or data incident with known, demonstrated limits.
problem: The checked-in migration baseline contains CLI output, and CI documents a schema-push workaround. Historical local security and QA evidence cannot prove current deployment recovery. This feature is operational infrastructure with an internal runbook interface, not a new pupil dashboard. It must make the difference between a backup existing, a backup being restorable and a school being ready to reopen explicit. The two operational screens are optional runbook or review-tool visualizations; delivery may use existing dashboards, CI reports or documented procedures rather than building new application panels.
scope: Replace the invalid migration baseline with an agreed, verified history and test clean provisioning plus upgrades from supported versions.
Inventory database, object storage, configuration and encryption dependencies required for a complete recovery.
Schedule and document isolated restoration rehearsals using synthetic or approved appropriately protected data.
Add deployment gates for migration checks, critical workflows, integrity reconciliation and a documented forward-recovery decision.
Record backup age, actual restored point, elapsed recovery time, integrity findings and operator sign-off.
outOfScope: Claiming a contractual recovery target before measurements and operating commitments exist.
Allowing school staff to run destructive production restore operations.
acceptance: A clean environment provisions successfully from versioned migrations without manual schema edits.
Every supported upgrade path passes on a representative populated staging database with reconciliation checks.
A rehearsal restores both records and referenced files into an isolated destination that cannot send real notifications.
The run report states the actual recovery point and elapsed time rather than assuming provider plan guarantees.
A failed migration or verification gate prevents release promotion and preserves diagnostic evidence.
Production restoration requires recorded operator authorization, destination confirmation and an approved incident procedure.
qa: Upgrade a populated database with existing grades, invoices and attachments from the prior release.
Restore a backup whose object-storage reference is missing and confirm the rehearsal fails clearly.
Interrupt a migration at an identified failure point and exercise the documented recovery route.
successMetric: All supported migration paths pass; every scheduled restore rehearsal has measured recovery time, verified records/files and an accountable owner.

principles: Use an operator checklist with evidence links, not a reassuring green backup badge.
Make environment and destination impossible to confuse during consequential actions.
Distinguish rehearsal, readiness and incident execution in the interface.

screens.name: Recovery readiness
screens.purpose: Internal operations view showing restore evidence, backup freshness and release readiness for each environment. It helps an operator identify missing proof without exposing pupil records or secret connection values.

screens.name: Rehearsal result
screens.purpose: Document the complete recovery sequence and blocking discrepancies. The final decision requires actual restored-record and file checks, with a path to a remediation issue rather than a one-click production replacement.

states.empty: No successful rehearsal; say recovery is unverified and link the prerequisite checklist.
states.loading: Show the current stage and elapsed time without inventing a completion percentage.
states.error: Preserve logs and the isolated destination for authorized diagnosis; mark readiness blocked.
states.permission: Only operational roles can execute; school administrators receive a plain service update when relevant.
states.success: Record measured recovery evidence and reviewer sign-off, without promising untested availability.

ux.mobile: Provide a read-friendly incident checklist on mobile; require deliberate confirmation for operator actions and avoid tiny dense log tables.
ux.rtl: Mirror operator labels if localized; keep timestamps with explicit zone, commands and evidence hashes isolated LTR.
ux.accessibility: Checklist stages have semantic headings and text results; logs are expandable and searchable without a keyboard trap.
copy: Restore completed. Verification is still pending.
Release blocked: file reconciliation did not pass.

userStory: As an authorized academic or finance reviewer, I want corrections to preserve original values and reasons so that families and auditors can understand how an official record changed.
problem: Grade and finance workflows already write audit records, but a shared correction experience should preserve meaning across reports, invoices, receipts and exported documents. A correction is not merely an edit icon: it needs a before/after preview, current-version protection and domain-specific consequences. Financial entries often require a reversal or adjustment rather than rewriting history, while released grades require a new approved report version.
scope: Define correction commands for marks and finance records with immutable original reference, reason, actor and timestamp.
Require before/after review and current-record version checks before committing consequential changes.
Route published grades through renewed approval and financial changes through appropriate adjustment or reversal entries.
Separate correction requester and approver where school policy requires it, preventing self-approval for those cases.
Expose a redacted understandable history and correction receipt while keeping internal notes restricted.
outOfScope: Inventing universal accounting rules or replacing country-specific finance requirements.
Deleting original audit entries to simplify the activity timeline.
acceptance: Every correction retains the original record and links its successor or compensating transaction.
A missing reason or stale record version prevents commitment and preserves the user’s draft.
Published mark changes require the report-version approval path before family visibility.
Financial corrections reconcile balances and do not silently rewrite an already issued receipt.
Policies requiring a second approver reject self-approval through both UI and direct API requests.
An authorized reviewer can reconstruct values, reasons and actors without reading application logs.
qa: Two staff request different changes to the same mark and the second sees a stale-version conflict.
Reverse a partially allocated payment and reconcile all affected invoice balances.
Review a family-visible correction history containing a restricted internal note.
successMetric: One hundred percent of consequential corrections have traceable before/after evidence; track approval time and unresolved reconciliation exceptions.

principles: Present the consequence in domain language before asking for confirmation.
Keep original and proposed values adjacent with explicit units and currency.
Distinguish public explanation from private reviewer notes.

screens.name: Request correction
screens.purpose: Staff propose a specific change against the current record and see downstream effects before submission. The form adapts to grades or money while retaining one recognizable correction structure.

screens.name: Correction history
screens.purpose: Review a record’s successive approved changes and linked receipts. The view separates the initial record from later corrections and shows which version is currently authoritative without discarding earlier evidence.

states.empty: No corrections; show the original record and explain when a formal correction is necessary.
states.loading: Preserve the proposed change while impact calculations load; do not enable approval until complete.
states.error: Show the changed underlying value and ask the requester to review their proposal again.
states.permission: Explain which reviewer can approve; never make lack of access look like missing history.
states.success: Provide a correction reference, updated authoritative version and status of any downstream review.

ux.mobile: Stack original and proposed values with labels; use a fixed review summary that does not cover reason fields or the keyboard.
ux.rtl: Mirror the timeline and form while isolating currency amounts, identifiers and mathematical comparisons.
ux.accessibility: Do not use strikethrough alone for previous values; announce totals and validation changes and preserve focus after approval.
copy: This change will create report version 3 for review.
Correction recorded. The original receipt remains in history.

userStory: As the platform AI owner and school administrator, I want approved provider policies, controlled data handling and recorded evaluation so that AI features remain accountable and manual school work continues when AI is unavailable.
problem: The provider switchboard and pseudonymization exist, but free-text fields can preserve identifiers, the scanner is Pakistan-specific and invalid provider-order configuration can reintroduce a public fallback. These are source findings to remediate and test, not evidence of a live disclosure. A configurable Ollama URL alone also does not prove local processing. Build one gateway that validates actual destinations, complete prompts, allowed features and review requirements. The two operational screens are optional runbook or review-tool visualizations; delivery may use existing dashboards, CI reports or documented procedures rather than building new application panels.
scope: Define an explicit provider/destination allowlist with school policy, region requirements and approved fallback behavior; invalid configuration fails closed.
Minimize structured context and scan the complete outbound payload including free text, attachments and source excerpts using reviewed multilingual cases.
Centralize feature policy, prompt/source versions, request budgets, evaluation metadata and required human approval.
Evaluate generated questions, answer keys, remarks and translations on educator-reviewed sets with documented failure thresholds.
Provide safe degraded behavior preserving manual authoring, saved drafts and transparent quota/service messages.
Record redacted operational evidence and retention controls without logging raw sensitive prompts by default.
outOfScope: Claiming anonymization, regulatory certification or local-only processing solely from a provider name.
Autonomous consequential decisions or training providers on school data without an explicit approved arrangement.
acceptance: Only approved actual destinations receive requests; malformed or unknown provider settings never activate a public fallback.
The full outbound payload is checked, including identifiers embedded in free text and non-Pakistani formats.
Denied payloads and provider failures do not expose raw sensitive content through logs or user errors.
Each generated artifact records the model, prompt, source and policy versions needed for review.
Required educator evaluation checks pass before a new model/prompt version is promoted.
Budgets and rate limits prevent unauthorized excess usage without disabling non-AI school tasks.
Human approval requirements remain enforced by the authoritative publication service, not a model instruction alone.
qa: Insert a guardian name and Saudi-style phone into a free-text generation prompt.
Configure an invalid provider order and a remote Ollama destination under a local-only school policy.
Promote a model that fails Arabic answer-key checks and verify rollout remains blocked.
successMetric: Track blocked unsafe payload tests, educator-reviewed quality failures, approved-draft rate, latency and cost per completed workflow.

principles: Operational AI controls show actual processing destinations and policy decisions.
School users receive plain explanations and manual alternatives, not vendor stack traces.
Evaluation results distinguish content quality, privacy controls and availability.

screens.name: AI policy
screens.purpose: Authorized operators configure the actual processing destination, allowed features and fallback policy. The view should make data-routing consequences inspectable without displaying secrets or suggesting that every provider label implies a hosting guarantee.

screens.name: Evaluation release
screens.purpose: Review educator and privacy test evidence for a proposed model or prompt release. Failed cases link to redacted examples and remediation; a passing latency chart cannot compensate for an unsafe data or answer-key failure.

states.empty: No approved provider policy; disable generation and offer manual authoring with an administrator setup route.
states.loading: Keep saved drafts visible while a request runs; record genuine job progress only.
states.error: Use a neutral explanation with retry or manual continuation; never echo raw provider payloads.
states.permission: Only policy owners change destinations; educators can review permitted content without secret access.
states.success: Confirm the policy/evaluation version and what features may now use it.

ux.mobile: School users see concise AI state and manual options; operator policy/evaluation screens support review on mobile without exposing dense secret configuration.
ux.rtl: Use Arabic educator-reviewed examples and bidirectional identifier tests; keep destination hosts, versions and numeric budgets isolated LTR.
ux.accessibility: Errors and review states have text labels; tables are keyboard navigable and evaluation evidence is available as readable text.
copy: AI drafting is unavailable. You can continue writing manually.
Release blocked: two answer keys failed educator review.

userStory: As a school staff member, I want the status and next action for a report batch or message delivery so that I know what completed and can recover failures without repeating successful work.
problem: Workers, notification records and delivery fields exist, but accepting a request is not proof that a recipient received it. Build one understandable job-status contract on the durable orchestration dependency. It should distinguish queued work, completed processing, provider acceptance and delivery evidence, while preventing manual retries from generating duplicate reports or messages.
scope: Define user-facing job and recipient states with timestamps, counts and links to source records.
Expose resumable progress for imports, PDF generation and report delivery using the durable job identifier.
Allow authorized retry of failed items only, preserving idempotency and the original approved report version.
Show actionable failure categories such as missing contact, invalid file, provider outage and expired authorization.
Record cancellation requests honestly: completed work remains completed and already sent messages cannot be unsent.
outOfScope: Implementing the underlying outbox, owned by F70.
Claiming read receipts where the chosen channel does not supply them.
acceptance: A batch’s item counts reconcile with queued, running, completed, failed and cancelled outcomes.
Retrying failed recipients does not resend successful recipients or substitute a newer unapproved report.
Refreshing or changing devices reopens the same persisted job status.
Provider accepted, delivered and read remain separate states with only supported evidence shown.
A school user cannot read or retry another tenant’s job through its identifier.
Cancellation explains which items had already completed and produces an auditable outcome.
qa: Retry a 100-recipient batch with 97 successes and three different failure reasons.
Restart a worker while PDFs are being created and reopen the progress view.
Receive late duplicate provider callbacks after a user has requested cancellation.
successMetric: Track time to recover failed items, oldest unresolved job age and duplicate delivery rate; require reconciled counts on every test batch.

principles: Show progress as accountable counts rather than an optimistic success toast.
Put the recovery action beside the reason it is needed.
Do not make teachers learn provider error codes to retry a report.

screens.name: Job activity
screens.purpose: Staff see the jobs they are allowed to manage with actual completion counts and meaningful next steps. Long-running work stays visible after navigation and links back to the original class or process.
notes: Do not equate queued with sent

screens.name: Delivery recovery
screens.purpose: Inspect recipient-level failures without repeating successful sends. Contact corrections are saved through the proper pupil or guardian workflow; this screen retries only the approved delivery job.

states.empty: No recent jobs; explain where report, import and communication work will appear.
states.loading: Keep current totals visible while polling or reconnecting; show the last update time.
states.error: If status cannot refresh, say it is unknown and prevent blind duplicate starts.
states.permission: Read-only staff see results without retry or cancellation controls.
states.success: Show reconciled counts and outstanding exceptions, with a durable receipt.

ux.mobile: Use stacked job cards and recipient details; primary retry remains tied to selected failed items with a count.
ux.rtl: Mirror queue layout; retain LTR phone, email and job references with clear channel labels.
ux.accessibility: Announce phase changes, not every polling update; status icons have text and keyboard-selectable rows.
copy: 97 delivered. Three families need attention.
Retry requested for two failed deliveries.

userStory: As a teacher completing a long form, I want navigation, refresh and connection problems to preserve my work so that an interruption does not force me to re-enter it.
problem: Existing unsaved-change helpers and role layouts provide a base, while imported issues report form refresh loss and inconsistent navigation. Draft recovery must distinguish local unsaved input from confirmed server data. It also needs explicit expiration and account boundaries so a shared school computer never restores one person’s draft into another account. Accessibility should be repaired in shared components and verified in real task flows.
scope: Inventory long forms and implement a consistent saved, saving, unsaved and recovery contract using the shared design system.
Persist permitted drafts with account, school, record and schema-version boundaries plus an explicit retention policy.
Handle back, refresh, route changes and concurrent record updates without silently discarding edits.
Replace disruptive full-page transitions with stable shells and meaningful panel loading states.
Audit keyboard, focus, labels, contrast and error summaries on onboarding, admission, marks and settings flows.
outOfScope: Full offline transactional synchronization, owned by the offline feature.
Persisting secrets, payment credentials or unrestricted confidential notes in browser storage.
acceptance: Refreshing an eligible form restores its same-account draft with a visible last-saved time and review choice.
Signing out or switching accounts cannot reveal the former account’s local draft.
When the server record changed, recovery shows conflicting fields and requires an explicit resolution.
All modal flows support keyboard entry, contained focus and focus return to their trigger.
Validation provides field messages and an error summary without clearing valid input.
Primary navigation preserves context and shows the active section consistently across roles.
qa: Enter a long admission draft, refresh, then switch accounts on the same browser.
Recover a draft after another staff member changes the underlying pupil record.
Complete a marks-and-review flow using keyboard only at increased text size.
successMetric: Measure lost-draft incidents and recovery completion; require zero critical keyboard or labeling failures on the designated task paths.

principles: Saving indicators must describe actual durability, not imply server confirmation.
Preserve familiar navigation while reducing full-screen interruption.
Ask about discarding work only when unsaved changes genuinely exist.

screens.name: Admission draft
screens.purpose: A long form keeps its section navigation, completion status and reliable draft indicator visible. Staff can move between sections without treating each movement as a submission or losing entered details.
notes: Save status next to primary action

screens.name: Recover your work
screens.purpose: Compare a recovered draft with current server values before applying it. Resolve conflicts field by field and give a clear discard option that removes only the draft, never the existing school record.

states.empty: No saved draft; start from current server values and explain when recovery becomes available.
states.loading: Show the form shell while fetching the record; never replace an active edited form with a spinner.
states.error: Keep input and show whether the latest change exists locally, on the server or nowhere durable.
states.permission: A revoked account cannot restore restricted records; discard local protected drafts safely.
states.success: Confirm that the server accepted the record and clear the corresponding draft only afterward.

ux.mobile: Single-column sections retain progress and save state; keyboard appearance must not cover errors or submission controls.
ux.rtl: Use logical spacing and mirrored section navigation; isolate email/phone fields without reversing cursor behavior.
ux.accessibility: Use persistent labels, visible focus, readable solid text colors and non-color error markers; test 200% text scaling.
copy: Draft saved on this device at 10:42.
This record changed. Review three fields before restoring.

userStory: As a registrar, I want a permanent pupil identity with dated enrollments so that transfers, promotions and changes of roll number preserve accurate academic and financial history.
problem: The current Student model links directly to a current class/campus and already has admission number, timeline and class history. Global school groups need a clearer distinction between the person and each enrollment period. A name or roll number must not become identity, and moving a pupil must not rewrite the historical context of a report, invoice or attendance entry.
scope: Define immutable internal pupil identity and scoped institution identifiers separate from year/class roll numbers.
Represent enrollment periods with institution, campus, curriculum, class, status and effective dates.
Make transfers and promotion create reviewed enrollment transitions with referential history retained.
Provide a registrar timeline joining identity, enrollment and source documents while restricting confidential fields.
Implement duplicate review and carefully authorized identity consolidation with a dry-run dependency report and auditable outcome.
outOfScope: Automatically sharing records between unrelated schools merely because identifiers or names match.
Rewriting historical reports to use the pupil’s current class or grading rules.
acceptance: A pupil keeps the same permitted permanent identity when class, roll number or campus changes.
Historical attendance, reports and invoices retain their original enrollment context after a transfer.
Overlapping enrollments are validated against explicit school policy and never silently created.
Two pupils with the same name remain distinct in search, imports, family linking and AI context.
A duplicate consolidation preview lists affected records and blocks incompatible or unauthorized merges.
A registrar can reconstruct the pupil’s dated path using timeline events and their source records.
qa: Promote a pupil with published reports and unpaid prior-year fees.
Transfer between campuses on a mid-term date and check attendance boundaries.
Review two same-name pupils with different guardians and prevent accidental consolidation.
successMetric: Zero historical record relabeling after transition tests; measure duplicate resolution time and enrollment exceptions per intake.

principles: Keep permanent identity visible but secondary to the pupil’s readable name.
Show current placement separately from the chronological record.
Make effective dates and historical consequences explicit before a transfer.

screens.name: Pupil record
screens.purpose: The registrar sees current enrollment at the top and dated transitions below it. Each past placement links to the appropriate period’s records, avoiding the impression that all history belongs to the current class.

screens.name: Transfer review
screens.purpose: Preview a proposed enrollment transition and the records that remain with the prior period. The registrar confirms identity, target placement and effective date before any downstream timetable or family views change.

states.empty: No enrollment yet; show identity details and a controlled create-enrollment action.
states.loading: Keep the identity header visible while history loads with date-ordered placeholders.
states.error: A conflicting transition stops the operation and highlights overlapping dates.
states.permission: Registrars manage transitions; families see only authorized historical summaries.
states.success: Confirm the new enrollment and list historical records preserved unchanged.

ux.mobile: Timeline becomes chronological cards with an always-visible current-placement summary; transfers use a short step form.
ux.rtl: Mirror timeline alignment and isolate pupil IDs; localized academic-year labels retain unambiguous start/end dates.
ux.accessibility: Use semantic chronology and descriptive links; do not depend on visual timeline position to communicate sequence.
copy: Transfer changes current enrollment; past reports remain unchanged.
Pupil ST-0042 is enrolled in West 7B from 12 October.

userStory: As a school data administrator, I want to preview, reconcile and safely reverse a bulk import so that correcting a spreadsheet does not require repairing hundreds of records manually.
problem: Bulk pupil import and financial bank import already exist, but a consistent staged reconciliation and rollback contract is missing. Different imports carry different consequences: an unchanged new roster can be reversed, while records already used in invoices or grades need guarded compensation. The experience must distinguish file parsing from committed changes and must never suggest that uploading a file immediately made authoritative records.
scope: Introduce a staged import batch with file fingerprint, mapped columns, target scope, validation results and row-level decisions.
Preview additions, updates, duplicates and rejected rows with explicit match keys and downloadable corrections.
Validate dates, currencies, identity links and references using the target institution’s configuration before committing.
Commit reviewed batches idempotently with per-row results and an audit link; resume interrupted jobs without duplication.
Provide reversal eligibility analysis and compensating correction guidance when later records reference imported data.
outOfScope: Automatic acceptance of fuzzy identity matches or silent merging of similar pupil names.
Unrestricted database restore as the normal import undo button.
acceptance: Uploading and validating a file does not mutate live student, finance or enrollment records.
A duplicate file or repeated commit returns the same logical batch outcome rather than duplicate records.
The preview reconciles input row counts with accepted, rejected, skipped and unresolved categories.
Ambiguous identity matches require a staff choice using stable identifiers, not automatic full-name matching.
Only validated, explicitly selected rows commit; the final receipt lists every row outcome.
Reversal refuses destructive deletion of referenced records and explains the affected dependencies with a correction route.
qa: Import a mixed file containing duplicate pupils, an invalid date and an unknown class.
Disconnect after commit starts, reopen the batch and retry without duplicate rows.
Attempt reversal after an imported pupil receives a published result and invoice.
successMetric: Track time from upload to reconciled commit, unresolved-row rate and post-import corrections; require zero silent duplicate creation in retry tests.

principles: Expose match rules and counts before the final commit action.
Keep the source row beside the proposed record when resolving an ambiguity.
Use precise verbs: Upload, Validate, Commit and Reverse have different effects.

screens.name: Import preview
screens.purpose: Show the proposed changes grouped by issue severity and allow staff to fix mappings or exclude rows without losing the staged file. The summary reconciles every source row before the commit step.
notes: No commit with unresolved selected rows

screens.name: Batch receipt
screens.purpose: A durable import receipt shows what actually committed and whether reversal remains safe. Staff can inspect later dependencies before choosing an undo operation, and can export evidence for reconciliation.

states.empty: No import batch; offer a sample template and explain required stable identifiers.
states.loading: Show separate upload, validation and commit progress with retained row counts.
states.error: Keep the staged batch and identify affected rows; allow corrected re-upload with explicit rematching.
states.permission: Only authorized importers can commit; reviewers may inspect without a mutation action.
states.success: Display committed and skipped counts plus the receipt and reversal eligibility.

ux.mobile: Allow mobile receipt review and error download; complex column mapping remains a usable stacked form with an explicit larger-screen recommendation.
ux.rtl: Keep spreadsheet row numbers and identifiers LTR while mirroring explanatory panels and Arabic column names.
ux.accessibility: Errors link to the exact row and field; status summaries are announced once per phase and progress is not conveyed only by animation.
copy: 14 rows need attention before import.
126 records committed. Download the batch receipt.

userStory: As a school implementation lead, I want a guided setup that reconciles imported records and shows readiness so that I can begin a real class workflow without guessing what remains unfinished.
problem: The onboarding wizard and many settings already exist, but setup should be a durable implementation journey rather than one long success animation. Schools arrive with inconsistent spreadsheets, missing guardian links and unresolved opening balances. The workflow must separate essential first-class configuration from optional modules and record reconciliation evidence before claiming the institution is ready.
scope: Create a persistent setup checklist based on institution type, enabled modules, country and curriculum choices.
Guide creation of one campus, academic structure, class and staff assignments before broad module activation.
Connect staged imports to a reconciliation summary covering pupils, guardians, staff and selected opening balances.
Provide a synthetic practice mode and a first-class walkthrough clearly separated from live records.
Let an authorized lead mark readiness only after required checks pass and record unresolved optional work with owners.
outOfScope: An unconditional same-day migration promise or automatic activation of every optional module.
Country-specific curriculum design, owned by the localization and curriculum configuration features.
acceptance: Setup resumes at the last completed step after refresh or changing authorized implementation staff.
Required fields and dependencies reflect the selected institution configuration, not only Pakistan defaults.
Imported counts and unresolved guardian/class relationships are visible before readiness approval.
Practice records are visibly synthetic and cannot send messages or produce real financial entries.
The first-class walkthrough reaches attendance, assessment setup and family preview using configured data.
Completing setup records the approver, time and outstanding optional tasks without hiding them.
qa: Configure a two-campus school with different calendars and one shared teacher.
Reconcile an import with missing guardian links and a pupil assigned to an unknown class.
Leave midway through setup, return on mobile and complete only the required first-class steps.
successMetric: Measure time to first verified class workflow and number of reconciliation issues discovered after go-live.

principles: Present the next necessary decision and defer optional configuration.
Use readiness evidence rather than a percentage that treats all tasks as equal.
Show the institution scope consistently when moving between setup and module settings.

screens.name: School readiness
screens.purpose: An implementation home shows the next required task, blocked dependencies and optional follow-ups. It lets the school expand progressively without mistaking a partially completed import for a usable pupil register.
notes: Resume links open the exact step

screens.name: Reconcile before start
screens.purpose: Compare source totals with configured records and resolve discrepancies before the lead approves live use. The review names the missing relationship or balance rather than showing a generic setup failure.
notes: No approval while required checks fail

states.empty: New institution; explain the first-class goal and offer a short setup path.
states.loading: Keep completed checklist items visible as readiness checks refresh.
states.error: Failed imports remain recoverable with exact batch links and counts.
states.permission: Only authorized leads approve readiness; other staff see tasks assigned to them.
states.success: Show verified live readiness, practice completion and next optional setup separately.

ux.mobile: Checklist and simple configuration work on mobile; dense reconciliation becomes cards with source and system counts adjacent.
ux.rtl: Mirror the step flow and localize examples; use explicit timezone and currency labels in configuration summaries.
ux.accessibility: Step headings expose completion text; progress does not depend on color and focus moves to the first validation issue.
copy: Four guardian links need review before family access.
Your first class is ready. Review optional setup next.

userStory: As an admissions officer, I want configurable applications and a clear enquiry-to-enrollment process so that families give information once and each application has an accountable next step.
problem: Admission queries, follow-ups and a pupil admission form exist, but they need a single application identity and controlled conversion into enrollment. Different schools require different questions and documents. Requiredness must be configurable without turning every form into an unstructured survey, and an admitted child must not be duplicated when a staff member retries enrollment or imports a later spreadsheet.
scope: Add versioned application form configuration with reusable identity fields, conditional sections and required document rules.
Track enquiry, application, review, offer, waitlist, acceptance and conversion with owner and next-contact date.
Offer a mobile family application link with draft recovery, submission receipt and limited status access.
Detect possible duplicates using configured stable identifiers and require staff review before merging or conversion.
Convert accepted applications to permanent pupil/enrollment records transactionally while preserving submitted form versions and consent evidence.
outOfScope: Automated admissions ranking or decisions based on sensitive characteristics.
A general-purpose public survey builder unrelated to school admission.
acceptance: Publishing a revised form does not alter answers or requiredness of previously submitted application versions.
Families can save and resume permitted drafts and receive a stable submission reference.
The pipeline identifies unassigned applications and overdue follow-ups without exposing them to students or unrelated guardians.
Required document and conditional field rules are validated on the server as well as in the form.
Repeated conversion of the same accepted application creates one pupil/enrollment outcome.
Potential duplicate identities require an explicit authorized choice with linked history.
qa: Submit under form version one while an administrator publishes version two.
Retry conversion after a network interruption and confirm one enrollment.
Complete an Arabic application on mobile with missing required and optional documents.
successMetric: Track application completion, time waiting for the next staff action and duplicate enrollment rate after conversion.

principles: Families see clear requirements and progress without internal admissions notes.
Staff work from ownership and next action, not an ambiguous card color.
Separate offer acceptance from creation of the authoritative pupil record.

screens.name: Admissions pipeline
screens.purpose: Office staff prioritize applications by stage, ownership and missing requirements. A list view remains available alongside stage filters so keyboard users can manage the same work without drag-only interactions.

screens.name: Application review
screens.purpose: Review submitted answers against the exact form version and enrollment target. Missing files and possible duplicate records appear before the final conversion, with confidential office notes kept distinct from family messages.

states.empty: No applications for this intake; offer the published form link or create an enquiry.
states.loading: Keep the selected application and stage visible while documents load.
states.error: Preserve review notes and explain failed upload or conversion without losing the submitted application.
states.permission: Admissions staff see private notes; families see only their own submission and permitted status.
states.success: Issue an enrollment reference linked to the original application and record the conversion owner.

ux.mobile: Family forms are mobile-first with upload progress and resumable sections; office reviews use stacked requirement cards on small screens.
ux.rtl: Localize form labels and conditional help; isolate application IDs and contact fields while mirroring step order.
ux.accessibility: Every required field is programmatically identified; conditional sections announce changes and errors link to the exact question.
copy: Your application is saved. Two required documents remain.
Enrollment created from application APP-042.

userStory: As a teacher, I want one approved resource library with precise audience and version controls so that learners and families can find the right materials without receiving staff-only answers or outdated documents.
problem: Pupil and staff document records, upload signing and chat attachments exist, but they do not form a curriculum resource library. Learning content needs its own version, objective mappings, audience and review state. A handout, school policy and answer key may look like similar files while carrying very different sharing rules. The library must also supply trustworthy source references to generation and study-assistant features.
scope: Create resource records with file/link content, owner, source/license information, version, language, accessibility metadata and review state.
Assign curriculum objectives and intended classes, groups, guardians or staff audiences with a sharing preview.
Support secure upload, content-type/size validation, safe processing and recoverable storage failures.
Publish approved resource versions and retain stable references for assignments, generated questions and policy citations.
Provide learner/family access, search and download views that enforce current membership and resource audience rules.
Handle replacement and retirement without silently changing material pinned to existing assessments or assignments.
outOfScope: A public copyrighted textbook repository or unrestricted web scraping.
Replacing pupil administrative document custody or physical library circulation.
acceptance: Every published resource identifies its owner, audience and exact version, including files linked from assignments.
A staff-only answer key is excluded from learner search, previews, direct downloads and AI source retrieval.
Upload failure or unsafe content prevents publication and leaves a clear recoverable draft state.
Replacing content creates a successor version while existing pinned references remain reproducible.
Revoked membership or changed audience prevents new access, with signed-link expiry behavior documented and tested.
Teachers can preview what a selected class or guardian audience will see before publishing.
Resource descriptions and accessible alternatives are available when a format cannot be previewed inline.
qa: Upload an answer key beside a pupil handout and inspect both through student search and direct links.
Replace a resource used in a published quiz and verify the original citation still resolves correctly.
Interrupt a large file upload on mobile, resume or retry and confirm one resource version.
successMetric: Measure successful resource access, upload recovery and incidents of outdated or incorrectly shared materials; require no answer-key leakage in role tests.

principles: Audience is a first-class publishing decision, not a hidden advanced setting.
Show version and curriculum context where teachers reuse a resource.
Offer an accessible reading route instead of requiring every user to open a PDF.

screens.name: Learning resources
screens.purpose: Teachers find and manage approved class resources with audience and version visible in the list. The same catalogue can present a restricted learner view without exposing staff metadata or answer-key names.
notes: Pin version when used in assessment

screens.name: Publish resource
screens.purpose: Before publication, the teacher checks the resource preview, source rights and actual recipient scope. The review highlights answer-key classification and missing accessibility information so a file cannot be casually shared with the wrong group.
notes: Do not expose file storage URLs

states.empty: No resources for this class; teachers can add approved material while learners see a plain availability message.
states.loading: Show upload progress and processing state separately; retain the resource draft if navigation occurs.
states.error: Explain file, permission or storage failure with retry and preserved metadata.
states.permission: Denied resource access reveals no restricted title or answer content and offers a relevant staff contact.
states.success: Confirm published version and audience, with a preview of the learner-visible resource.

ux.mobile: Learners and parents get readable cards and low-bandwidth download choices; teacher uploads use native file selection with clear progress.
ux.rtl: Mirror catalogue and forms; render resource language independently and isolate filenames, URLs and scientific notation.
ux.accessibility: Require descriptive link names, keyboard file controls, readable HTML descriptions and accessible alternatives for essential image/audio content.
copy: Only Class 7A learners can open this published handout.
Version 2 published. Existing quiz citations still use version 1.

userStory: As an authorized school staff member, I want predictable search and filters across school records so that I can find the correct pupil, family, class or document without guessing exact wording.
problem: Existing directories, filters and a teacher command palette provide separate search experiences, and imported issues report filtering defects. Global search must be an authorized index of useful records rather than an accidental cross-school directory. Similar names need stable contextual identifiers, and zero results must be distinguishable from restrictive filters or a temporarily unavailable source. Actions should open the original workspace rather than duplicate editing inside search.
scope: Define supported record types and searchable fields with role, tenant, campus and child-scoped filtering before ranking or counting.
Standardize text normalization, exact identifier search, filter semantics, sort order, pagination and URL-restorable state.
Show disambiguating class, campus, year and stable identifiers without exposing unrelated confidential fields.
Provide keyboard search navigation and source deep links that preserve the caller’s permitted context.
Measure and repair stale results after updates, enrollment changes, archiving and permission revocation.
Keep family/student search limited to authorized tasks and resources rather than the full staff directory.
outOfScope: Indexing private safeguarding notes, raw AI prompts or unrestricted message bodies by default.
A parallel record editor or fuzzy automatic identity merger inside search.
acceptance: Results, suggestions and counts exclude unauthorized records before presentation and do not leak their existence.
Searching a stable pupil identifier returns the correct authorized record despite name changes.
Combined filters have documented AND/OR semantics and remain visible when results are empty.
Clearing filters restores predictable results, and refresh/back navigation restores the same search state.
Archived and historical records appear only through explicit permitted filters with clear labels.
Updates and revocations converge within a documented tested indexing window; stale links recheck current authorization.
Every result opens the authoritative module and identifies enough context to distinguish namesakes.
qa: Search two same-name pupils in different campuses using both a partial name and a stable ID.
Combine class, status and academic-year filters, then clear only one and navigate back.
Revoke access to a resource that is already present in cached search suggestions.
successMetric: Measure successful record-finding tasks, zero-result recovery and stale/unauthorized result defects against a representative scoped fixture set.

principles: Always expose active filters and scope before declaring that nothing exists.
Rank exact identifiers clearly and disambiguate names without excessive personal detail.
Search finds the record; its original module remains responsible for editing.

screens.name: Search school records
screens.purpose: Staff search within a visible institution/campus scope and compare contextual results. Compact type filters and explicit chips prevent hidden filter combinations from creating confusing empty screens.

screens.name: No matching records
screens.purpose: A useful zero-result state explains the exact active filters and offers safe ways to broaden the query. It never suggests that inaccessible records exist, and preserves the original input while the user changes one constraint at a time.

states.empty: No matches in the displayed authorized scope; show active filters and safe query suggestions.
states.loading: Keep the query and filters stable, cancel stale requests and mark source-specific loading.
states.error: If a source fails, label results partial and offer retry without clearing the query.
states.permission: Unauthorized records never appear; direct stale links are rechecked in the destination module.
states.success: Open the exact record and restore the previous query, filters and selected row on return.

ux.mobile: Use a focused search sheet with compact result cards; keep filter chips visible and avoid a tiny desktop-style multi-column table.
ux.rtl: Support Arabic normalization deliberately without corrupting exact IDs; mirror result alignment and isolate Latin identifiers and mixed-script names.
ux.accessibility: Provide labeled search, keyboard result navigation, announced result counts and a clear escape route from the command palette.
copy: No matches with Class 7B selected. Clear that filter to try again.
Results are partial: the resource library could not refresh.

userStory: As a curriculum lead, I want lessons and assessment items mapped to versioned learning objectives so that coverage and follow-up refer to what pupils were actually expected to learn.
problem: Subjects and syllabus topics exist, but a topic name alone is too broad to support meaningful assessment blueprints or misconception analysis. A school may follow different curricula at different stages, and the same objective can appear in several resources. Establish a lightweight objective hierarchy with source provenance and effective versions, while avoiding claims of mastery from a single total mark or merely scheduled teaching.
scope: Extend syllabus topics with stable objective identifiers, descriptions, prerequisite links, curriculum version and approved source references.
Map objectives to classes, teaching periods, approved resources and later assessment items without duplicating objective identities.
Support reviewed import of curriculum structures and local additions with provenance and conflict handling.
Show planned, taught and assessed coverage separately with the evidence behind each state.
Preserve objective versions on existing assessments when curriculum wording or structure changes.
outOfScope: Automatic certification that a school complies with an external curriculum.
Student mastery prediction without sufficient item-level evidence and educator interpretation.
acceptance: Every objective has a stable identifier, curriculum context and a clear learner-oriented description.
Moving or renaming an objective does not break linked resources or historically versioned assessment items.
Coverage distinguishes scheduled teaching, teacher-recorded delivery and actual assessment evidence.
Unmapped questions and resources are visible as review work rather than silently assigned by title similarity.
Imported duplicates require a reviewed match using identifiers and version information.
Teachers only edit objectives permitted by their curriculum role, while authorized leads approve structural changes.
qa: Import two curriculum versions with the same code but changed objective wording.
Map one resource to two objectives and check coverage counts avoid duplicate evidence.
Rename a topic after a paper is published and inspect the original assessment blueprint.
successMetric: Measure assessment items with reviewed objective mappings and time needed to identify uncovered required objectives.

principles: Organize by the teacher’s subject and teaching period before exposing curriculum administration.
Show the source and evidence behind each coverage indicator.
Do not equate a checked teaching box with demonstrated pupil understanding.

screens.name: Objective map
screens.purpose: A curriculum workspace displays concise objectives and their current teaching/assessment coverage. Filters help teachers find the objectives relevant to their class without navigating a large national framework tree.

screens.name: Objective evidence
screens.purpose: Inspect the resources, delivered lessons and assessment items supporting an objective. The lead can correct mappings and see historical versions before approving a curriculum change that affects future planning.

states.empty: No objectives in this subject; offer a reviewed import or a small manual starting set.
states.loading: Retain subject filters while loading objective branches and evidence counts.
states.error: Invalid prerequisite cycles or duplicate codes are explained before saving.
states.permission: Teachers can link permitted resources; curriculum structure edits require the appropriate role.
states.success: Confirm the objective version and show which future mappings are affected.

ux.mobile: Objective lists become readable cards; editing uses a short form and avoids requiring a wide hierarchy canvas.
ux.rtl: Mirror hierarchy controls, preserve curriculum codes and mathematical expressions as isolated segments, and support Arabic objective descriptions.
ux.accessibility: Provide a table alternative to hierarchy trees, keyboard expand/collapse and text equivalents for coverage graphics.
copy: Taught in two lessons; assessment evidence is still missing.
Objective v2 saved. Existing published papers retain v1.

userStory: As an assessment lead, I want a reviewed, versioned question bank and paper blueprint so that teachers reuse reliable questions and can verify coverage before students encounter an assessment.
problem: The exam pipeline records aggregate marks but does not yet define questions, answers, rubrics or objective-level assessment composition. Build the shared assessment domain before paper generation, OCR and online attempts diverge. Question reuse needs provenance, review status, controlled answer visibility and fixed versions in released papers; later edits must never change an assessment pupils have already taken.
scope: Define item types, content, answer keys, scoring rubrics, objective tags, source/license metadata and immutable reviewed versions.
Build question authoring and peer/lead review with draft, reviewed, retired and restricted states.
Create blueprints specifying objective coverage, marks, duration and question-type distribution with explicit validation.
Assemble assessment versions from pinned question versions and produce controlled paper/online representations.
Provide duplicate/similarity review and usage history without exposing active assessment answers to learners.
outOfScope: Public question marketplace or external teacher-sharing network.
Claiming calibrated difficulty or equivalent variants before sufficient response evidence exists.
acceptance: Only reviewed eligible item versions can be included in a releasable assessment version.
An item edit creates a draft successor and leaves already issued papers and attempts unchanged.
Blueprint totals reconcile item marks, coverage and configured assessment duration assumptions.
Teacher-only answer and rubric fields cannot be retrieved through learner endpoints or resource previews.
Question provenance and allowed use are recorded before sharing outside its original private scope.
Retiring an item prevents future selection while preserving historical assessments and marking evidence.
qa: Edit an answer key after a paper has been published and inspect the original issued version.
Assemble a blueprint with an uncovered objective and mismatched marks total.
Attempt to fetch a restricted answer using a student account and a known question identifier.
successMetric: Track reuse of reviewed items, blueprint blockers caught before release and question defects reported after administration.

principles: Separate question quality review from assembling a particular paper.
Make version and answer visibility easy to inspect at the point of reuse.
Show coverage gaps as specific missing objectives rather than a vague readiness score.

screens.name: Reviewed question bank
screens.purpose: Teachers find reusable items using curriculum, objective, type and review status. The table emphasizes eligible versions and marks, with usage details available before adding an item to a paper.

screens.name: Blueprint review
screens.purpose: The lead checks the proposed paper against its intended curriculum coverage and scoring plan. Each item is pinned to a reviewed version, and unresolved gaps prevent the draft being treated as ready for release.
notes: Do not auto-fill from unreviewed items

states.empty: No reviewed questions match; offer authoring or change filters without showing unauthorized items.
states.loading: Keep selected questions visible while filtering or recalculating blueprint totals.
states.error: Explain missing marks, invalid answer schema or stale item version without losing the paper draft.
states.permission: Review and release permissions differ from ordinary authoring; locked answer fields remain protected.
states.success: Confirm the approved blueprint and pinned item versions with remaining assessment setup steps.

ux.mobile: Question search becomes cards with objective, marks and state; blueprint totals stay visible above the selected-item list.
ux.rtl: Mirror bank/filter layout; isolate question IDs, equations and option markers while supporting Arabic source and item text.
ux.accessibility: Question selection works with keyboard and checkboxes; all item content has text alternatives and rubric tables expose headers.
copy: Two marks of Comparison coverage are still missing.
Blueprint approved with six reviewed question versions.

userStory: As a teacher, I want an editable quiz draft grounded in selected approved materials so that I can prepare an appropriate assessment faster while checking its sources, answers and coverage.
problem: AI currently generates remarks, lesson plans and other drafts, but no assessment item generation workflow exists.
