A useful test generator needs more than a prompt box: it must start from a reviewed blueprint and available source material, create structured editable questions, and make uncertainty visible. Generated difficulty is an estimate, citations must resolve to actual source passages, and approval must remain a teacher action before paper or online release.
currentEvidence: No question-generation or learner-attempt model found in the reviewed source
scope: Create a generator flow from reviewed objective coverage, question-type mix, marks, duration, language and approved source versions.
Return structured draft items with answers, explanations, marking guidance and resolvable source references.
Validate required fields, marks totals, duplicate items, answer consistency and supported mathematical expressions before review.
Allow item-level editing, rejection and targeted regeneration without replacing teacher-approved items.
Record generation policy/model/prompt versions and teacher approval before adding reviewed items to an assessment version.
outOfScope: Automatic publication, final grading or guaranteed equivalence between generated paper variants.
Training on school material or fetching unapproved copyrighted content as an implicit fallback.
acceptance: Every generated item references a selected source passage or is explicitly marked unsupported and blocked from approval.
The draft conforms to the chosen blueprint or reports which constraints could not be satisfied.
Teachers can change a question, answer and rubric together, with stale answer references flagged.
Regenerating one rejected item preserves approved questions and records the new draft version.
The interface labels estimated difficulty and never represents it as measured item calibration.
A provider outage or budget limit leaves manual question authoring and saved drafts usable.

Generated questions, answers and rubrics remain drafts until an authorized teacher approves their exact version; neither UI nor direct API can publish or distribute unapproved content. Teacher answer keys and private source annotations remain excluded from student outputs until their separate configured release conditions are met.
qa: Use an unsupported source, then attempt to publish or distribute its generated draft through both UI and direct API before teacher approval; verify release is rejected and the source gap remains visible.
Edit a question’s numbers and ensure its answer/rubric requires renewed review.
Interrupt a long generation job after several items complete and resume the saved draft.
successMetric: Measure teacher acceptance without revision, invalid/unsupported item rate and time to an approved paper, including review and corrections.

principles: Grounding and review status must be visible per question, not buried in a global disclaimer.
Let teachers control the blueprint before generation and preserve their edits.
Treat a confident-looking answer as a draft until it passes substantive review.

screens.name: Generate assessment
screens.purpose: The teacher defines a constrained draft using approved curriculum resources. A compact blueprint preview shows coverage and totals before generation, with estimated processing cost and a manual-authoring route.

screens.name: Question review
screens.purpose: Review one draft item beside its source evidence, answer and marking guidance. Teachers accept or revise each component, and unsupported claims are blockers rather than decorative warning badges.

states.empty: No reviewed blueprint or sources; link to those prerequisites and retain any settings already entered.
states.loading: Show item-level progress and saved drafts; generation acceptance is not content approval.
states.error: Report missing evidence or service failure precisely, with manual editing and retry of only unfinished items.
states.permission: Only assigned academic staff generate from permitted resources; answer keys remain staff-only.
states.success: Confirm approved item count, remaining blockers and the exact assessment draft version.

ux.mobile: Teachers can review a question and source sequentially on mobile; desktop uses a split view with synchronized evidence links.
ux.rtl: Generate in the selected language; render Arabic questions RTL while isolating equations, Latin terms and numeric answer options correctly.
ux.accessibility: Use semantic question structures, accessible math where supported, labeled answer options and source links that return focus to the reviewed item.
copy: No selected source supports this objective. Add material or revise the blueprint.

userStory: As an examination officer, I want dates, rooms, seating and invigilators checked together so that a published examination plan is feasible for every affected pupil and staff member.
problem: Examination sessions, room capacity, seating and conflict helpers are substantial existing capabilities. The next step is one coherent planning and publication experience rather than adding another calendar. Formal office examinations and teacher classroom quizzes must retain their different permissions. Capacity warnings need to include usable seating and accommodations, and schedule changes must produce a versioned update for the right audiences.
scope: Unify session planning with dated papers, candidate enrollment, usable room capacity and permitted invigilator assignments.
Evaluate pupil, teacher, room and timetable conflicts before draft approval and again at publication.
Represent split rooms, accessibility seating and authorized accommodation timing without publicly exposing support details.
Provide accessible seating/date-sheet previews and versioned exports linked to the exact published session.
Make post-publication changes show affected candidates, staff and documents before issuing controlled updates.
outOfScope: Building online exam attempts or secure-browser behavior in this scheduling feature.
Automatically optimizing an entire institution timetable without human review.
acceptance: A paper cannot publish with unresolved hard conflicts in candidate, room or invigilator schedules.
Split-room allocations reconcile every candidate exactly once and respect usable capacity.
Restricted accommodation details are visible only to authorized staff while required scheduling effects are honored.
Printed date sheets and seating exports identify the same published session version.
Changing a published paper creates a reviewed version and an explicit list of affected recipients.
Teacher quiz permissions cannot bypass office control over formal examination sessions.
qa: Schedule overlapping papers for pupils taking different elective combinations.
Reduce a room’s usable seats after a draft allocation and attempt publication.
Extend one candidate’s authorized timing and check invigilator/room overlap warnings.
successMetric: Measure unresolved conflicts at publication and time to produce a reconciled datesheet; require zero duplicate or unseated candidates.

principles: Keep constraints beside the schedule so officers see why a choice is unavailable.
Use a compact table alternative to every calendar or seating canvas.
Distinguish draft planning from the family-visible published version.

screens.name: Exam planning
screens.purpose: Officers coordinate paper times and room allocations with a persistent conflict list. The calendar is a planning aid; each paper also has an editable table row and a clear draft/publication state.
notes: Do not rely on drag to schedule

screens.name: Publication checks
screens.purpose: Review candidate coverage, capacity and staff availability before issuing the datesheet. Each blocker links to the responsible paper or allocation, while the publication summary identifies exactly who will receive changes.

states.empty: No papers planned; create the first paper from an authorized exam definition.
states.loading: Keep the selected session visible while recalculating constraints; mark suggestions temporarily stale.
states.error: Show conflicting resources and safe alternatives; preserve the draft schedule.
states.permission: Office staff publish formal sessions; teachers see only permitted quizzes and assigned duties.
states.success: Confirm version, recipient scope and export availability with delivery tracking links.

ux.mobile: Mobile staff see their duties and paper details first; officers can use a table/list editor instead of the wide calendar.
ux.rtl: Mirror calendar labels carefully while preserving chronological time order; keep seat and room codes isolated LTR.
ux.accessibility: Offer keyboard room/seat assignment controls and a textual seating list; conflict icons always include a reason.
copy: One invigilator is already assigned at this time.
Datesheet v2 published for 126 candidates.

userStory: As a teacher, I want to photograph a structured marks sheet, verify uncertain cells and approve a reconciled import so that I save transcription time without surrendering control of official marks.
problem: No OCR, OMR or QR assessment scanning implementation was found. Existing marks validation and exam locking provide a good destination, but extraction must be a separate staged process. QR should identify an opaque assessment/template reference; it does not recognize handwriting or prove authority. The initial scope is teacher-recorded numeric marks on a known template, with explicit review, duplicate handling and a reversible batch receipt.
currentEvidence: No assessment scanning workflow found in current source
scope: Generate versioned structured marks sheets with opaque QR references, roster snapshot, subject/question limits and page numbers.
Capture or upload images with orientation, blur, crop and completeness checks before extraction.
Extract numeric cells and absent markers into a staging batch, retaining image crops and confidence evidence for review.
Validate identity, roster membership, allowed marks, totals, duplicates and current exam state before teacher approval.
Commit approved changes through the shared marks service with before/after preview, idempotency and reversible import receipt.
Record extraction corrections for quality measurement without using pupil images for model training by default.
outOfScope: Autonomous grading of essays or arbitrary handwritten mathematical reasoning.
Treating OCR confidence as proof that a mark or pupil identity is correct.
acceptance: A valid QR resolves only inside authorized school scope and contains no plaintext pupil personal data.
An image with missing pages, severe blur or unreadable references cannot silently proceed as a complete batch.

Confidence only prioritizes review and never automatically approves or commits marks. Every uncertain or invalid cell requires explicit review beside its original image crop; high-confidence cells remain reviewable in the batch preview, and every committed batch requires recorded teacher approval.
Values outside configured limits, mismatched rosters and locked exams block commitment with actionable explanations.
Scanning the same page twice does not duplicate grades; changed rescans require a reviewed before/after decision.
Only approved cells enter the gradebook, with batch identity, teacher, original evidence and correction history retained.
The resulting marks still require normal exam/report approval before family visibility.
qa: Scan a tilted sheet with an ambiguous 7/1 digit, one confidently misread numeric cell, an absent pupil and a missing page; verify confidence cannot bypass review or teacher-approved commitment.
Rescan a corrected page while another teacher has changed one of its marks.
Attempt import after the exam is locked or its roster changes.
successMetric: Measure verified cell accuracy, review burden, uncorrected transcription errors and minutes per class including rescans and correction time.

principles: Put the original crop beside the editable extracted mark at every review point.
Use confidence to prioritize review, never to disguise unverified official data.
Keep capture, extraction, review and commit as visibly different stages.

screens.name: Scan review
screens.purpose: A teacher checks the captured sheet against extracted values with the selected cell crop enlarged. The main navigation advances through required reviews first, while allowing every supposedly confident value to be inspected.

screens.name: Approve marks import
screens.purpose: The final preview reconciles pages, roster and grade changes before writing anything. Staff see existing marks and proposed replacements, including explicit conflicts with changes made after the scan began.

states.empty: No scan yet; offer the correct printable template and a short capture example.
states.loading: Show upload and extraction separately, saving completed pages before further work.
states.error: Explain blur, missing page or roster mismatch with retake, replace or resolve actions.
states.permission: Only staff assigned to the exam can review and import; QR possession grants no access.
states.success: Show committed count, skipped/conflicted cells and the import receipt; results remain unpublished.

ux.mobile: Camera capture is mobile-first with a large preview and retake control; cell review stacks crop above input with a fixed Next button.
ux.rtl: Mirror review panels while preserving table-template coordinates; isolate numeric marks and opaque IDs without changing extraction orientation.
ux.accessibility: Provide file upload as a camera alternative, large readable crops, keyboard cell navigation and text descriptions of every validation blocker.
copy: Please confirm this digit: 1 or 7.
24 marks imported. Review and publish results through the usual workflow.

userStory: As a teacher or guardian, I want permitted conversations and attachments to send reliably with recoverable status so that important school communication does not disappear or reach the wrong family.
problem: The chat domain already has relationship policies, attachments, realtime streams, read state and school settings. Improve its reliability rather than building a second messaging system. Reconnects, retried sends, changed class relationships and failed uploads must have clear outcomes. A read marker should not be confused with completion of a school request, and private school messages should not spill into notification previews.
scope: Unify persisted send identifiers, retry semantics and reconciliation between optimistic messages and server-confirmed history.
Make attachment upload, validation, association and download authorization robust across interrupted connections and membership changes.
Reconnect realtime streams with gap recovery so messages and unread counts converge without duplicates.
Expose failed/pending/delivered states accurately and keep read acknowledgement distinct from task completion.
Apply current school relationship policy to conversation discovery, sending, members and attachment access.
Respect quiet hours and safe notification previews while preserving access to urgent school actions through the appropriate workflow.
outOfScope: Opening pupil-to-pupil or parent-to-parent messaging by default.
Automatic monitoring that labels students or treats message sentiment as a safeguarding diagnosis.
acceptance: Retrying a pending message with the same send identifier creates one authoritative message.
After reconnect, the thread and unread count match persisted server state with no missing sequence gap.
An attachment cannot be sent before successful validation/storage and cannot be retrieved outside current authorized scope.
Relationship changes prevent newly forbidden communication without leaking conversation previews in search.
Failed sends preserve draft text and attachment state with an explicit retry or remove action.
Quiet-hour behavior follows school and recipient policy, and urgent exceptions are explicit rather than silently inferred.
Read status never marks a separate consent, payment or report-review action complete.
qa: Send a message, lose the acknowledgement and retry after reconnect.
Remove a teacher’s class relationship while an old attachment link is open.
Upload a disallowed file and a valid large file from a slow mobile connection.
successMetric: Measure missing/duplicate message incidents, attachment completion and reconnection recovery; track unresolved failed sends separately from unread messages.

principles: Never present an optimistic bubble as confirmed delivery.
Keep recovery attached to the affected message rather than a fleeting global toast.
Make recipient context obvious before sending sensitive school information.

screens.name: School conversation
screens.purpose: A familiar thread shows the verified recipient relationship, concise messages and trustworthy send states. Failed messages remain at their original position with their own recovery action, preserving the conversation context.

screens.name: Recover attachment
screens.purpose: The sender sees each attachment’s processing state and can retry the failed upload without duplicating the message. Access checks and file validation are explained plainly, with a safe option to send the text separately.

states.empty: No messages yet; name the permitted participants and offer a school-appropriate starting action.
states.loading: Keep existing history and draft visible during reconnect; show the last synchronized point.
states.error: Display retry on the failed message or file and explain whether anything was actually sent.
states.permission: If access changes, stop new sends and show a neutral explanation without expanding the address book.
states.success: Confirm server acceptance and update delivery/read states only when evidence arrives.

ux.mobile: Messaging is mobile-first with a reachable composer, upload progress above the keyboard and no controls hidden beneath safe-area insets.
ux.rtl: Align message layout by sender while rendering each message’s language correctly; isolate filenames, links and times within Arabic text.
ux.accessibility: New messages announce politely without stealing focus; attachment controls have names and the composer supports keyboard send alternatives.
copy: Upload failed. Your message draft is still here.
Message sent. Reading it does not complete the linked school request.

userStory: As a principal, I want one prioritized queue of unresolved school work with an owner and next action so that important tasks are completed instead of disappearing inside separate dashboards.
problem: Principal dashboards, notifications and AI summaries exist, but a summary does not establish an accountable work item. The queue should be driven by explicit source conditions such as missing attendance, pending report approval and failed delivery. AI may explain the evidence but must not invent urgency, close tasks or turn fee difficulty into a judgment about a child.
scope: Define actionable item types with source record, deterministic trigger, owner, due time and resolution condition.
Aggregate attendance, report approval and delivery exceptions from the dependent modules without duplicating their authoritative state.
Allow assignment, acknowledgement and justified snooze while preserving overdue visibility and audit history.
Deep-link each task to its exact resolution workspace and reconcile closure from the actual source outcome.
Provide campus and responsibility filters with a transparent explanation of sorting and urgency.
outOfScope: Autonomous AI actions changing grades, finances, staffing or pupil classifications.
A second generic task manager disconnected from source school records.
acceptance: Every item identifies its originating record, trigger, owner and supported next action.
Resolving a source issue closes or updates the queue item without requiring duplicate manual completion.
Opening the same underlying exception through different channels does not create duplicate active work items.
Snoozing requires a reason and return time, and overdue items remain discoverable.
Campus and role restrictions apply to queue summaries and deep links alike.
Sorting explains urgent categories and does not silently use an opaque pupil risk score.
qa: Complete attendance from the teacher workspace while a principal has the queue open.
Snooze a report blocker until tomorrow and trigger a publication deadline today.
Open an old notification after its source exception has already been resolved.
successMetric: Measure median exception age, overdue unresolved work and percentage resolved through the linked source action.

principles: Put the next useful action ahead of charts and overall counts.
Show why an item exists and who is responsible without blame-oriented language.
Keep resolved work available as evidence without crowding the active queue.

screens.name: Principal queue
screens.purpose: A concise list shows work requiring attention today, grouped by responsibility and due time. The principal can distinguish an overdue administrative task from a pupil support concern without reading an AI-generated narrative.

screens.name: Action detail
screens.purpose: The detail view explains the trigger and offers the source-specific next step. Assignment and snooze are secondary actions; actual completion comes from the authoritative workflow so the queue cannot hide unresolved school work.

states.empty: No unresolved items in this scope; show when sources were checked and a route to resolved history.
states.loading: Retain filters and prior items with a refreshing label; avoid flashing an empty success state.
states.error: Show which source feed failed and mark totals incomplete until recovery.
states.permission: A task outside the caller’s scope gives a neutral denial, not a preview of its confidential details.
states.success: Confirm the actual source resolution and remove the active item while preserving history.

ux.mobile: Use a mobile-first action list with thumb-friendly primary actions; dense evidence expands only on demand.
ux.rtl: Mirror list and evidence order; keep due times explicit in the school timezone and identifiers isolated.
ux.accessibility: Queue items have descriptive link names, visible keyboard focus and text urgency labels; live updates do not steal focus.
copy: Three report versions still need approval.
Resolved in Report Review. This action is now complete.

userStory: As a teacher or student-support lead, I want a concern linked to a specific intervention, responsible adult and reassessment so that support continues until its outcome is reviewed.
problem: The existing intervention model stores recommendations and approval but lacks structured goals, owners, due dates and measured outcomes. An AI paragraph should not become a permanent label on a child. Build evidence-based, time-bounded support using assessed work and appropriate family involvement. Progress must distinguish participation, task completion and comparable reassessment, without treating correlation as proof that the intervention caused improvement.
scope: Add structured concern evidence, baseline, goal, owner, planned activity, review date and approval to intervention records.
Link question-level learning evidence and approved family actions without exposing unrelated financial or confidential support details.
Provide check-ins for assigned staff and record actual participation, adjustments and pupil feedback.
Schedule a comparable reassessment or documented review and capture its result alongside the baseline.
Close, extend or escalate the intervention through a human decision with a reason and retained history.
outOfScope: Automated diagnoses, disciplinary decisions or fixed ability labels based on scores.
Claiming causal learning gains from an uncontrolled before/after comparison.
acceptance: Every activated intervention has an owner, specific goal, source evidence and review date.
Only authorized reviewers can activate suggested plans; AI output remains an editable draft.
Missed check-ins remain visible to the owner and principal queue until resolved or rescheduled.
Families see only explicitly shared goals/actions, not private professional notes.
Outcome review distinguishes baseline, follow-up evidence, completion and contextual limitations.
Closing or extending a plan records a human decision and preserves prior plan versions.
qa: Create support for a misconception supported by two items rather than an overall average.
Change the responsible teacher mid-plan and verify follow-up ownership transfers.
Review improved scores when attendance changed and record the limitation without a causal claim.
successMetric: Measure activated plans with timely check-ins and completed outcome reviews; separately report learning evidence and participation.

principles: Use supportive, specific language about skills and actions rather than labeling children.
Put the next check-in and responsible adult above AI narrative.
Show what is shared with the family before approval.

screens.name: Support plan
screens.purpose: The teacher converts a concrete concern into a manageable support plan. Evidence, goal and owner are required; generated suggestions are editable and kept visually separate from the approved action.

screens.name: Outcome review
screens.purpose: Compare the starting evidence with a later review while recording what was actually delivered. The reviewer can continue, adjust or close the plan and should see missing evidence before drawing conclusions.

states.empty: No active plan; start from a selected concern or create a specific support goal.
states.loading: Keep plan details visible while linked evidence loads; mark missing sources clearly.
states.error: Preserve check-in notes and prevent an outcome decision based on unavailable evidence.
states.permission: Restricted professional notes remain hidden from families and unrelated staff.
states.success: Confirm the decision, next owner/date and precisely which family update was shared.

ux.mobile: Teachers can record short check-ins on mobile; families receive a concise action card rather than the internal case workspace.
ux.rtl: Mirror timeline and form; keep assessment fractions and dates isolated and avoid negative labels in translated copy.
ux.accessibility: Goals and evidence are available as text, charts have equivalents and status changes are announced without focus theft.
copy: Goal: explain equivalent fractions using two examples.
Review complete. Continue practice until 29 October.

userStory: As a cover coordinator, I want an absence to produce a feasible substitute plan and a checked catch-up task so that the school preserves teaching continuity rather than only recording missed lessons.
problem: Staff leave, availability, timetables and AI lesson drafts exist, but a connected substitution and missed-learning recovery workflow does not. Availability alone is insufficient: qualifications, workload, supervision requirements and campus travel matter. Suggested cover must remain a reviewed proposal, and a missed lesson should produce a concrete teaching handover rather than an unsupported assumption that pupils learned the topic.
scope: Translate approved absence dates into affected lessons and an accountable cover request.
Suggest eligible substitutes using availability, teaching suitability, workload and campus constraints with visible reasons.
Let coordinators approve partial coverage, record unresolved lessons and issue controlled timetable updates.
Attach the original teacher’s approved lesson resources and concise handover instructions to each covered lesson.
Create a reviewed missed-learning recovery task when coverage changes the planned learning, and track completion in the student agenda.
outOfScope: Automatic staffing commitments or punitive teacher performance judgments.
A claim that generated substitute lessons guarantee equivalent learning outcomes.
acceptance: Each approved absence identifies affected lessons using current published timetable versions.
Suggestions explain eligibility and reject timetable conflicts or required qualification mismatches.
Approving cover rechecks availability and fails safely if another coordinator has already assigned the teacher.
Substitutes receive only authorized class resources and duties for the covered period.
Uncovered or materially changed lessons create an explicit follow-up decision rather than appearing completed.
Family/student updates reflect only approved changes and link to the correct lesson or catch-up task.
qa: Two coordinators simultaneously assign the same substitute to different lessons.
An absent teacher works across campuses with travel time constraints.
A lesson is supervised but its practical activity is postponed; create and complete catch-up work.
successMetric: Track uncovered teaching periods, coordinator time per absence and percentage of missed-learning follow-ups completed.

principles: Explain why a teacher is suggested instead of presenting an opaque ranking.
Separate covering the room from delivering the planned learning.
Keep urgent same-day scheduling concise and defer optional handover detail.

screens.name: Cover required
screens.purpose: The coordinator sees affected lessons and the reason each remains uncovered. Suggestions show relevant constraints, allowing a quick decision without opening several staff and timetable pages.

screens.name: Lesson handover
screens.purpose: Confirm the substitute, resources and expected learning before publication. If the original objective cannot be taught, the coordinator records the actual activity and assigns a follow-up owner instead of marking it as delivered.

states.empty: No uncovered lessons; retain upcoming approved absences and recently resolved cover.
states.loading: Keep the absence impact list while eligibility checks run.
states.error: Explain the newly conflicting assignment and preserve the proposed handover.
states.permission: Only coordinators commit cover; substitutes can acknowledge their assigned duties.
states.success: Confirm affected timetable versions and notification jobs; show remaining uncovered lessons.

ux.mobile: A same-day mobile cover list prioritizes time, room and handover action; full planning remains productive on desktop.
ux.rtl: Mirror panels and localize dates while keeping lesson chronology, room codes and resource filenames readable.
ux.accessibility: Provide keyboard selection for substitutes and text conflict reasons; urgent tasks do not rely on flashing indicators.
copy: Teacher B is available and assigned to this subject.
Cover approved. One lesson still needs a follow-up plan.

userStory: As a school-group leader, I want shared policy templates with controlled campus overrides so that campuses follow group standards while retaining explicitly permitted local differences.
problem: Multi-campus institutions and local settings already exist, but there is no established versioned inheritance model for group policy. Simply copying values creates drift, while forcing one configuration can violate a campus’s valid calendar, curriculum or operating needs. The design must show the effective value, its source and the consequence of a group change before applying it.
scope: Define versioned templates for approved configurable domains with effective dates and explicit override permissions.
Display inherited, overridden and locked values distinctly at campus level, including a reason and author for overrides.
Preview the effect of a template update across campuses and identify incompatible curriculum or calendar settings.
Require an authorized review process for overrides and material group policy changes.
Retain policy provenance on records that depend on it, avoiding retrospective alteration of published academic or financial artifacts.
outOfScope: One universal policy that automatically satisfies all countries or school types.
Retroactively recalculating old reports or invoices when a new template is published.
acceptance: Campus users can see the effective value and whether it comes from the group template or an approved override.
Locked fields reject changes through both UI and API, with a clear explanation and escalation route.
Publishing a new template shows affected campuses, preserved overrides and blocking incompatibilities.
An override records reason, approver, validity period and the template version it modifies.
Historical records retain the rules effective when they were produced.
A template can be staged for a future date and its activation is recorded with an auditable activation event.
qa: Publish a group grading change where one campus uses a different curriculum.
Expire an approved local override and verify the intended inherited value resumes.
Attempt a locked-field change by direct API while reviewing the same field in settings.
successMetric: Track unexplained configuration drift and time to review group changes; require complete provenance for every effective policy value.

principles: Always show effective values instead of making users mentally combine templates.
Explain locked and locally editable fields in ordinary school language.
Make a multi-campus impact preview mandatory before applying broad changes.

screens.name: Campus policy
screens.purpose: Campus administrators see the effective rules with their origins. A local override is a deliberate, reviewed exception and never appears identical to an inherited default.

screens.name: Group change review
screens.purpose: The group leader reviews the precise effect of a proposed template release across campuses. Conflicts and existing overrides remain visible before approval, avoiding silent replacement of legitimate local settings.

states.empty: No group template; explain whether current campus settings will become the initial baseline.
states.loading: Keep effective values visible while calculating proposed changes.
states.error: List affected campuses and prevent partial silent application when validation fails.
states.permission: Campus editors can request permitted overrides; only group policy owners publish templates.
states.success: Confirm the activation date, version and campuses requiring additional review.

ux.mobile: Campus policy is readable on mobile as setting cards; group impact tables offer stacked comparisons with a persistent affected count.
ux.rtl: Mirror inheritance indicators and isolate version identifiers; translate policy explanations rather than exposing internal keys.
ux.accessibility: Use text labels for inherited/overridden/locked states, and ensure disabled controls have an accessible reason nearby.
copy: This value is inherited from Group Policy v3.
Version 4 is scheduled. Two campus exceptions need review.
